changes.change: **The stairway.** Every plan climbs in weekly steps: small steps in the first half (standard 3 %), slightly bigger after the halfway week (standard 5 %), the hardest weeks last. When a muscle's level cap would be reached early, all its steps are scaled down by one factor λ so the planned peak lands on the cap in the final week. Replaces the 12-week acclimation cap (≤ 3 %), the 8-week "start hard" (start × 1.10, weeks 1-4 ≤ 5 %) and target-seeking.

**"Start at a 2, end at an 11"** is perceived overall load, not sets: each week shows a level from 2 to 11 that follows the stairway, and the planned effort drifts from 3 RIR to 1 RIR inside his 1-3 RIR band; lifters already at their caps get the "11" from load, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle.

**Never above 7 %/week planned; 10 % absolute.** Standard steps are 3-5 %; a "too easy" week adds 2 points (max 7 %); the person's total weekly resistance sets must rise by less than 10 %. A hand-set step runs 0-7 % (fixes 03's conflict 4).

**Check-in step table approved, minus the life column.** Effort mostly 1-6 → the planned step + 2 points (= his +7 % in the late half); effort 7-8 → the planned step (= his +5 % in the late half); effort 9 → hold; any 10 → hold and remove 1 set from that day; under half the sessions → repeat the week. The step is decided from **effort, completion and pain only**: the "life was harder / better" cells are dropped because he wants no lifestyle inputs (**flagged**).

**Retired:** the readiness score R (effort 40 / completion 20 / performance 20 / life 20), the intake "recovery signal" (sleep, stress, physical job), the 3 % default for stressed clients, "7 % only once logs earn it" and the "hold 2 weeks → deload" gate.
**No check-in = no adaptation:** the plan follows its planned stairway ("there is no data to go off of").

**Effort 10 = "the max I could do, but successful"** (0 RIR), not a fail; an optional separate 'Failed' answer is proposed. '8 - That was perfect' = hit the target the plan gave; '9' = harder than planned.

**Floor 10 sets a week per trained muscle; small muscles grow by the same idea.** Small-muscle starts L1 **10** (was 8) / L2 12 / L3 15; the level caps 14 / 22 / 25 now apply to every target muscle (small caps were 12 / 18 / 22); priority caps L1 18 / L2 26-28 / L3 30 approved; every cap is customizable; an optional **Pro** setting may let one priority muscle pass 30 (numbers PROPOSED).
**"Most people train 20-30 sets per muscle per week"**: researched (surveys of bodybuilders and gym-goers, dose-response meta-analyses, RP landmarks) and placed next to his statement.

**Rear delts:** own sets 4 / 6 / 8 approved. Reconciled with the floor of 10 by reading the floor on his SHOULDERS/TRAPS muscle group (rear + side delt work together) - INFERRED and **flagged** for round 3.

**Glute credit:** squats, lunges, deadlifts and RDLs give glutes **0.25** (hinges were 0.5 PROPOSED); hip thrusts and bridges 1.0; **KB swings are ballistic and never count as glute volume**; thruster = 1.0 quads + 0.5 shoulders + 0.25 glutes.

**No deload or maintenance week inside a block.** A block is completed; the deload (about half of the hardest week, same exercises, 3+ RIR) sits only between blocks. A block that cannot be completed is cancelled → maintenance phase (length chosen, extendable) → at its end the app asks: keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block. Triggered mid-block deloads are retired.

**R2-VOL-08 was not understood:** the default stays (alternate the first exercise between the two weekly exposures; bonus exercise on the optional day; with no optional day, on a day that already trains that muscle group) and is marked for a simpler re-ask.

**Full-body days: 2-4 exercises per muscle group that day, never 1.** Full-body days grow to 7-10 resistance exercises and 55-80 minutes; the time model adds a 1-minute changeover per exercise; the capacity table and every example were recomputed.
**Cardio count is adjustable** up or down by the user; aesthetics clients 4 (Orange, Green, Blue + a second Orange) plus optional 20-30-minute walks; athletes by sport off-season.

**Session rules:** heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days, non-axial alternatives on the other days, the counted list of axial lifts; light core opener (2 exercises × 2 sets short of failure) with optional core supersets or monster sets anywhere; field athletes 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block; athletic-template slots default to 2 sets (03's conflict 1); exercises by session length 45 ≈ 5, 60 ≈ 6-7, 75-90 ≈ 8-9 (03's conflict 6).

**Athletic budget:** plyo:ballistic shares by sport approved (end of block; each block starts 15 points more ballistic; share counted over jump **and** throw work); ballistic vs plyometric lists; "Receive-Create stages" (1 Land, 2 Land & Go, 3 Repeat) with their week timing; Olympic lifts up to 4 times a week (cleans on squat-pattern days, snatches on hinge days); full squat cleans/snatches 3-5 reps with the same weekly reps; % only when tested (RPE otherwise); in-season reductions for game-heavy sports; older adults (60+) no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default (optional with a warning); youth Olympic lifts from the floor from about 14 after a hang block; intermediates get the full Olympic scope (11's I14).
**Pre-season** = a 4-6-week block at about 60 % of off-season sets with more speed and power, then a 1-2-week taper; **maintenance** length is chosen and extendable.
**Year plan** = gen-pop "stay in shape" planning, fully tunable by the user (re-order blocks, more or less cardio, a winter powerlifting-style block; own calendar and holiday weeks).
**Tests** before the block (or in week 1) and at the end, never mid-block; untrained people never test a 1RM or a max mile from zero (5RM / 3RM or 80-90 % submax efforts).
**Next block** after a completed block: start × 1.05, cap + 1 (max 25 non-priority / 30 priority) approved; after a cancelled block: the same start (PROPOSED).

**"Stay athletic and active" gen-pop path** (pickleball, HYROX for fitness and similar, from the coach's request of 2026-10-08): uses the general-fitness volume factors and the floor of 10; its athletic work comes from the 04 sport profiles.

**Inconsistencies flagged by 03 and 11 fixed here:** priority add +4 (L1-L2) / +6 (L3) everywhere (I10); factor results round half up (I11); intermediates get the full Olympic scope (I14); the bodybuilder upper-body share is PROPOSED, not his number (I15); 8-9 exercises at 75-90 min is his VOL-08 answer (I16); hand-set step 0-7 % and RIR stays 1-3 (03 conflicts 2 and 4).

**Repeated week makes the block one week longer** (§3.7.3); **block-at-risk prompt** wording and triggers (§3.12).
**After a cancelled block, the new block starts at the same start** (§3.12).

**Floor of 10 for field athletes' chest and back** (raises 7.5 to 10; §3.4) and **small muscles on the same caps as big ones** (§3.3).
**Pro setting:** L3 only, one priority muscle, up to 35 sets, check-in required (§3.2).

**R2-SES-05 details:** groups = his FOCUS headers (shoulders together), calves keep one exercise × 3 sets per leg day, the generator consolidates a muscle onto fewer days rather than one exercise per day (§3.10).
**Time model:** 1-minute changeover per exercise (0.5 in a superset pair) on top of v1's per-set minutes (§3.10).
**R2-VOL-08 default** (to re-ask in plain words): alternate the first exercise between the two weekly exposures; bonus on the optional day, else on a day that already trains that muscle group (§3.9).
